customer.business: Chutney Tubes (Indian chutneys and sauces in 100g squeeze tubes)
customer.target: Urban Indian consumers (22 to 45) who eat parathas, samosas, momos, rolls, and tiffins 4+ times a week

behaviours.name: Daily Tiffin Packer
behaviours.how: Packs parathas, theplas, or rolls for office or college every morning and struggles with messy leaks or dry food.

behaviours.name: Quick-Commerce Spontaneous Snacker
behaviours.how: Orders samosas, momos, or rolls on Swiggy or Zomato and hates the watery, unhygienic polythene chutney pouch.

behaviours.name: Price & Value Sensitive
behaviours.how: Calculates cost per gram vs Maggi (₹14/100g) and Mother's Recipe (₹35/100g) and is skeptical of ₹99 for 100g.

behaviours.name: Label & Preservative Checker
behaviours.how: Reads ingredients lists, avoids artificial food coloring, and fears packaged green chutney tastes like vinegar.

behaviours.name: Brand Loyal & Homemade Defender
behaviours.how: Accustomed to home mixer-ground coriander chutney or standard Ching's/Veeba; skeptical of a new tube format.

behaviours.name: Foodie & Early Adopter
behaviours.how: Loves trying novel food hacks seen on Instagram Reels or Blinkit new arrivals and appreciates clever packaging.

objections: ₹99 for 100g feels steep when a 200g pouch of Mother's Recipe is ₹70 and 500g Maggi is ₹72

Will the flip-top nozzle get crusty and clogged after 3 days in the fridge?
Why order online and wait 2 to 3 days when I can grab sauce from the local kirana or make it at home?
Does watery liquid squirt out first before the thick chutney comes out?
My mother or cook already makes fresh green chutney in a dabba for free
100g is too small, that will finish in 4 or 5 parathas
habits: you pack a lunchbox with breakfast parathas before leaving for the metro at 8:30 AM
you order hot samosas from the neighbourhood mithai shop with 4 PM chai
you make quick late-night instant noodles, frozen momos, or frankies after work
you take road trips or train journeys on weekends and carry dry snacks
you order groceries 2-3 times a week on Blinkit or Zepto

pitch:
Chutney Tubes puts traditional Indian chutneys and sauces into clean 100g squeeze tubes with flip-top caps—no spoon, no spill, no sticky jar.

The line-up:
- Chaat Pair (₹179): Authentic Hari Chutney (mint-coriander) + Khatti-Meethi Imli Chutney.
- Single Tubes (₹99 each, 100g): Hari Chutney, Imli Chutney, Schezwan Sauce, Tandoori Mayo, Masala Ketchup, Garlic Mayo, Mint Mayo, Red Chilli-Garlic.
- 100% vegetarian, eggless, formulated for zero-mess tiffin and travel bags.

Available online with free delivery across India, or starter 2-pack at ₹179.
